items.title: 2.8 Elastic and inelastic collisions (elastic aur inelastic takkar) (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 2.8 with Figs. 2.10 to 2.14 and Example 2.8 (PDF 41-43, printed 38-40).

blocks.text: Jab tennis ki do balls takrati hain to collision ke baad woh pehle se kam velocity se rebound karti (wapas uchhalti) hain. Is dauran kinetic energy (K.E., motion ki energy) ka kuch hissa lost (zaya) ho jata hai: kuch friction (ragar) se, jab balls dabti (distort hoti) hain aur un ke molecules ek doosre par phisalte hain, aur kuch hissa heat (garmi) aur sound (awaz) energy ban jata hai.
Jis collision (takkar) mein system ki K.E. conserved (qaim, utni ki utni) na rahe, use inelastic collision kehte hain.
Kuch special (khaas) conditions mein collision mein koi kinetic energy lost nahi hoti.
Ideal (bilkul perfect) case mein jab koi K.E. lost na ho, collision perfectly elastic kehlata hai.

Example: hard (sakht) ball marble ke farsh par giraayi jaye to taqreeban usi height tak wapas uchhalti hai; farsh se collision mein bohat hi kam (negligible) energy khoti hai. Yaad rahe: momentum aur total energy har type ke collision mein conserved rehte hain, lekin K.E. sirf elastic collision mein conserved rehti hai.
Elastic Collisions in One Dimension (ek dimension mein elastic collision)

Do smooth (chikni), non-rotating (na ghoomne wali) balls lein jin ke mass m₁ aur m₂ hain aur jo shuru mein ek hi direction mein v₁ aur v₂ velocities se chal rahi hain. Woh takrati hain aur collision ke baad baghair ghoome usi straight line mein chalti hain. Collision ke baad un ki velocities v₁′ aur v₂′ hain (Fig. 2.10).

blocks.alt: Collision se pehle: balls m1 aur m2 velocities v1 aur v2 se right taraf. Collision ke baad: wahi balls velocities v'1 aur v'2 se right taraf.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.10: One dimension mein elastic collision, pehle aur baad (kitab ki Figure 2.10 ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.text: Right (daen) taraf ko velocity aur momentum ki positive direction lein. Momentum ke conservation se:
Collision elastic hai, is liye K.E. bhi conserved hai:
a² - b² = (a + b)(a - b) laga kar:

blocks.text_alt: or m₁(v₁ + v₁′)(v₁ - v₁′) = m₂(v₂′ + v₂)(v₂′ - v₂)   (2.30)

blocks.text: Ab Eq. (2.30) ko Eq. (2.29) se divide karein; m₁(v₁ - v₁′) aur m₂(v₂′ - v₂) dono taraf kat jate hain:

Collision se pehle (v₁ - v₂) pehli ball ki doosri ball ke hisaab se relative velocity hai, aur collision ke baad (v₁′ - v₂′). In ki magnitude barabar hai lekin direction ulat jati hai. Yani: relative velocity of approach (qareeb aane ki velocity) ki magnitude relative velocity of separation (door jane ki velocity) ke barabar hoti hai.
Equations (2.29) aur (2.30) mein m₁, m₂, v₁ aur v₂ known (maloom) hain. Inhen solve kar ke unknown v₁′ aur v₂′ nikalte hain:
Ab kuch special cases dekhte hain:
(i) Jab m₁ = m₂
Eq. (2.32) aur (2.33) mein m₁ = m₂ rakhne se:

blocks.latex: v_1' = v_2 \quad\text{and}\quad v_2' = v_1 \qquad (\text{as shown in Fig. 2.11})
blocks.text_alt: v₁′ = v₂ and v₂′ = v₁   (as shown in Fig. 2.11)

blocks.alt: case (i). Collision se pehle: barabar balls m1 aur m2 velocities v1 aur v2 se right taraf. Collision ke baad: m1 v'1 = v2 se aur m2 v'2 = v1 se chalti hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.11: Case (i), m1 = m2 (kitab ki Figure 2.11 ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.text: Yani barabar mass wali balls collision mein apni velocities aapas mein exchange kar leti (badal leti) hain.
(ii) Jab m₁ = m₂ aur v₂ = 0
Is case mein m₂ at rest (ruki hui) hai (v₂ = 0). Eqs. (2.32) aur (2.33) se:

Matlab m₁ collision ke baad ruk jati hai aur m₂ usi velocity se chal parti hai jo pehle m₁ ki thi (Fig. 2.12). Isi liye table par chalti billiard ball jab bilkul waisi ruki hui ball se takrati hai to pehli ruk jati hai aur doosri usi velocity se chal parti hai.

blocks.alt: case (ii). Collision se pehle: m1 v1 se m2 ki taraf chalti hai jo rest mein hai (v2 = 0). Collision ke baad: m1 ruk jati hai (v'1 = 0) aur m2 v'2 = v1 se chalti hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.12: Case (ii), m1 = m2 aur v2 = 0 (kitab ki Figure 2.12 ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.text: (iii) When a light body collides with a massive body at rest (jab halki body ruki hui bhaari body se takraye)
Yahan v₂ = 0 aur m₂ >> m₁ (m₂, m₁ se bohat bara). m₂ ke muqable m₁ ko neglect kar (chhor) sakte hain. Eq. (2.33) aur (2.32) se v₁′ = -v₁ aur v₂′ = 0.
Yani m₁ usi speed se wapas uchhalti hai aur m₂ apni jagah ruki rehti hai (Fig. 2.13). Squash player isi baat se faida uthata hai: ball deewar se usi speed se wapas aati hai.

blocks.alt: case (iii). Collision se pehle: chhoti ball m1 v1 se bohat bari ball m2 ki taraf chalti hai jo rest mein hai. Collision ke baad: m1 v'1 = -v1 se wapas aati hai aur m2 rest mein rehti hai (v'2 = 0).
blocks.caption: Figure 2.13: Case (iii), halki body rest wali bhaari body se takrati hai (kitab ki Figure 2.13 ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.text: (iv) When a massive body collides with light stationary body (jab bhaari body ruki hui halki body se takraye)

Yahan m₁ >> m₂ aur v₂ = 0, is liye Eqs. (2.32) aur (2.33) mein m₂ ko neglect kar sakte hain. Is se v₁′ ≈ v₁ aur v₂′ ≈ 2v₁. Yani bhaari body ki velocity taqreeban nahi badalti, lekin halki body aage ki taraf takrane wali body ki taqreeban double velocity se uchhal jati hai (Fig. 2.14).

blocks.alt: case (iv). Collision se pehle: bari ball m1 v1 se chhoti ball m2 ki taraf chalti hai jo rest mein hai. Collision ke baad: m1 taqreeban v1 se chalti rehti hai aur m2 taqreeban 2v1 se aage nikal jati hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 2.14: Case (iv), bhaari body rest wali halki body se takrati hai (kitab ki Figure 2.14 ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing).

blocks.title: Example 2.8
blocks.problem: 70 g ki ball 140 g ki doosri ball se takrati hai. Pehli ball ki initial velocity 9 m s⁻¹ right taraf hai aur doosri ruki hui hai. Agar collision perfectly elastic ho to collision ke baad dono balls ki velocity kya hogi?
steps: Given: m₁ = 70 g, v₁ = 9 m s⁻¹, m₂ = 140 g, v₂ = 0; maloom karna hai v₁′ aur v₂′.
v₂ = 0 hai, is liye (2.32) ka doosra term zero: v₁′ = ((m₁ - m₂)/(m₁ + m₂)) v₁ = ((70 - 140)/(70 + 140)) × 9 m s⁻¹ = (-70/210) × 9 m s⁻¹ = -3 m s⁻¹
Isi tarah (2.33) se: v₂′ = (2m₁/(m₁ + m₂)) v₁ = (140/210) × 9 m s⁻¹ = 6 m s⁻¹
blocks.answer: v₁′ = -3 m s⁻¹ (negative: pehli ball wapas left taraf jati hai) aur v₂′ = 6 m s⁻¹ right taraf.

blocks.prompt: Elastic aur inelastic collision mein farq batayein. Squash ki ball deewar se taqreeban usi speed se wapas kyun aati hai jis se takrati hai?
blocks.explanation: Elastic collision mein momentum aur kinetic energy dono conserved rehte hain; inelastic mein momentum conserved rehta hai lekin kuch kinetic energy heat, sound ya shakal bigarne (distortion) mein chali jati hai. Total energy aur momentum dono types mein conserved hain (neeche table dekhein). Ball halki hai aur deewar bhaari aur ruki hui, to case (iii) ke mutabiq v₁′ = -v₁ aur v₂′ = 0: ball usi speed se wapas aati hai aur deewar apni jagah rehti hai.

rows: Kinetic energy (K.E.) bhi conserved rehti hai
K.E. conserved nahi; kuch K.E. heat, sound aur distortion mein chali jati hai

Misal: tennis balls ki takkar, kam velocity se rebound

blocks.text: Summary (khulasa)

items: Inelastic: K.E. conserved nahi; perfectly elastic: koi K.E. lost nahi. Momentum aur total energy har collision mein conserved.

One-dimensional elastic collision: m₁(v₁ - v₁′) = m₂(v₂′ - v₂); v₁ + v₁′ = v₂′ + v₂ (relative speed of approach = relative speed of separation); v₁′ aur v₂′ ke formulas (2.32), (2.33); chaar special cases. Example 2.8: -3 m s⁻¹ aur 6 m s⁻¹.
